text:
Midday and the sky is spotless. It's already close to 50 and breezy out of the northwest, so with the sunshine it feels a bit cooler than the number. We're on track for a high near 51, a touch below normal for late October, but a jacket-and-sunglasses kind of afternoon. The sun sets a little before 6, and once it does, the temperature drops fast. Tonight is partly cloudy with a low right around 31, so expect frost on the windshield tomorrow morning.

High pressure is parked right on top of us, which is why this stretch is so quiet. Saturday starts chilly and ends up sunny and calm, with a high near 55. It's a good day for a long walk or a ride, and the lightest wind of the weekend. Saturday night stays clear and cold, with a low around 34.

Sunday is the warm one. Sunshine again, a south breeze picking up a bit, and a high near 61. The models are bunched between 59 and 63, so low 60s is a safe bet. Sunday night is milder, around 41.

There's no rain anywhere in this weekend, and a dry cold front on Monday should pass with next to nothing. Tuesday turns cooler again, so enjoy Sunday.

week.blurb: Sunny and crisp with a high near 51, then a chilly night around 31, so expect frost on the windshield.
Sunshine all day and a bit milder, with a high near 55, a lovely one for getting outside before the evening.
Sunny again and the warmest day of the stretch, with highs in the low 60s and a milder night near 41.
Mostly sunny and still mild with a high near 60, though it turns colder overnight, down around 36.
Looks like a sharp cooldown Tuesday, sunny but only near 48, with a frosty night in the upper 20s.
Trending a bit warmer Wednesday, mostly sunny with a high around 52 and a less frosty night in the mid 30s.
If the pattern holds, Thursday is mostly sunny and milder near 58, with clouds building in that evening.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-23T10:52:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Dry and seasonable weather to continue through early next week.
  2. Dry cold front to bring cooler temperatures on Tuesday and Wednesday with dry weather now expected to continue through much of next week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 227 AM EDT Friday... No significant changes have been made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure will continue to build across the North Country and northern New York today with the center of the high directly overhead on Saturday and the first half of Sunday. Below normal high temperatures, in the 48-52 degree range, are expected today with plentiful sunshine. Temperatures will moderate through the weekend with high temperatures by Sunday warming into the lower 60s. Dry weather will continue through Monday with the lack of any appreciable moisture or significant changes in the synoptic longwave pattern. KEY MESSAGE 2: Models continue to be less bullish on the upcoming cold front later on Monday. The latest suite of global guidance is showing a plethora of dry air ahead of the front which should allow the front to pass through the region with virtually no precipitation. A few members of the GEFS and ECMWF ensemble are showing a hundredth or two of precip at a few locations but the trend continues to be drier which makes sense given the current pattern. Another sharp cool down will be seen as we head into Friday with high temperatures struggling to warm into the mid to upper 40s even with abundant sunshine. Another 1030+ mb high pressure system will settle into the region on Tuesday with dry weather now expected through much of the week. A slight chance of rain has been added for Friday with a more amplified pattern with some moisture advection ahead of a stronger cold front. The dry air mass in place will be hard to displace so we will see how this pans out in a week from now.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Friday! Any clouds from yesterday afternoon and evening have come and gone at this point, and we are clear and cool to start off the day in the 20s and 30s once again. Plenty of sunshine into this afternoon will warm us back up into the upper 40s and 50s. More sunshine into the upcoming weekend as temperatures turn a tad warmer through the weekend. With that being said, Saturday starts cool with most waking up in the 20s, but plenty of sunshine will warm us into the 50s by Saturday afternoon. Sunshine persists into Sunday, and we warm back towards the 60s for Sunday afternoon. Dry weather continues right into next week. We may mix in more cloud cover for Monday as high temperatures head towards the upper 50s to lower 60s. Temperatures do turn a tad cooler for Tuesday, with afternoon high temperatures only in the 40s. Following that, milder air starts to return for Wednesday and Thursday as we see temperatures climb through the 50s and even back towards the 60s for Thursday. Again, we stay dry with a mixture of sunshine and clouds into next week.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-23T15:51:00Z — same caveat): Sunny days continue through the weekend, gradually turning warmer — Friday will feature lots of sun and temperatures in the lower 50s! This weekend will continue to have lots of sunshine. Highs reach the 50s Saturday, rebounding to the low and mid-60s for Sunday. Despite the enjoyable stretch, we'll have to watch for worsening drought and an increased brush fire risk due to the prolonged dry pattern.
